analysis.title: Global Rates Trader: Reaching Limits
key_insights: Tightening financial conditions, driven by wider credit spreads (especially European sovereign), tilt the scales toward long US and German duration. Wider spreads sketch out the boundary conditions for the recent sell-off.

The G4 sovereign bond rally late in the week came mainly from the return of European risk, with sovereign credit spreads widening sharply led by OATs. Softer US labor data added initial support for US yields. G4 front-ends reduced hike premium alongside dovish Fed and ECB communication.
The next US inflation print is the key test for the Fed path. GS still sees an asymmetry toward lower yields as fundamental support for duration builds.

US: GS economists moved the timing of the next and final Fed hike in their forecast to December. The September jobs report reinforced the view that the labor market is not a source of inflation pressure.

Widening credit spreads, most acutely in European sovereigns but also in US IG, introduce a correction mechanism to higher yields via tighter financial conditions. Middle East uncertainty and resilient AI investment plans contributed to the recent sell-off and are upside risks to GS's bullish yield view.

Vol: GS sees a plateau, not a peak. Implied vol is at the upper end of fair value given macro risks, which reduces the risk of further spikes. Unless yields stabilize, implied vol typically stays near highs after a large rates sell-off, especially on shorter tails. It retraces only after the local peak in yields.
Left-tail risks are becoming a more meaningful source of realized vol from current policy pricing. GS base case remains a grinding relief rally.

Micro factors (de-risking, negative convexity, CTD switch risk) played a supporting role in the sell-off. GS thinks their flow magnitude has diminished because mortgages are less negatively convex and asset managers have actively managed duration.

Treasury's expanded buybacks behaved as before. Treasury bought off-the-runs at prices cheap to market mid. The latest operation drew offer volumes 4x the previous two expanded buybacks. Buybacks have done little to lower yields, though spreads stayed well supported.
Attention is shifting to reducing long-end auction sizes, but with cheapening extending into the belly, issuance adjustments may not contain yields without macro tailwinds.

Canada: benign inflation should allow further reduction of front-end risk premium. US spillovers and energy prices will likely dictate CAD price action until the labor report and October BoC meeting. Governor Gravelle affirmed overnight repos as the main tool against upward CORRA pressure and the 50-70bn CAD reserves target range.

Europe: the return of sovereign risk (wider EMU spreads, flatter credit curve, lower Bund yields, weaker euro, equity underperformance) reduces near-term ECB tightening risk and shows a possible 'yield brake' on Bund yields. With growth robust and energy-driven inflation risk, front-end rates are unlikely to rally much further unless macro signals change.
GS sees an asymmetry to lower Bund yields via lower energy prices and hike risk, or via ongoing spread widening and safe-haven flows. 10y Bund forecast is 3.25% at end-2026.

10y OAT-Bund spread widened beyond 150bp before retracing to 140bp, levels last seen in the most acute phase of the 2011 European sovereign crisis. GS estimates OAT-Bund sensitivity to 1y-ahead deficit expectations at about 10bp per 1pt. Revised deficit expectations (0.4% and 0.5% of GDP for 2026 and 2027) explain only a small fraction of the widening.

The 50bp OAT widening in September would imply about 15ppt of GDP higher debt-to-GDP at the highest historical sensitivity (3bp/ppt). GS concludes the latest leg is driven by uncertainty and risk premium beyond fundamentals. OAT risk premium is priced higher and earlier than in previous political episodes.

Three routes to stabilize OAT spreads: global energy price relief, a successful 2027 budget keeping the deficit near the 5.0% objective or fiscal caution from presidential contenders, or financial conditions tightening enough to prompt an ECB response. The ECB hurdle to using its balance sheet (e.g. TPI) is high, but the first step is likely the ECB reiterating its tools are available.

Spillover from OATs to other EGBs rose, especially a sharp flattening of the Italian credit curve. Most spread markets still traded tighter than the overall spread move implies, so risk remains idiosyncratic to France. GS conviction on spreads is low. Longer-dated spreads are potentially the safer long given lower beta and Bund yield protection.

UK: Gilts have outperformed, and much of the rise in Gilt yields since June came from abroad. The BoE is likely to hike in November, but GS economists see enough slack to limit second-round effects, implying fewer hikes than priced. GS thinks Gilt outperformance can continue.

Japan: JGB swap spreads widened even as yields rose, so JGB supply is not the primary driver of the sell-off. GS attributes spread outperformance to falling long-end issuance, optimism on domestic demand (GPIF and NISA headlines), and a supportive global backdrop. Spreads are only slightly wide to fair value. Issuance and QT could raise free float about 5pp next year, pushing 10y fair value about 3bp tighter.

Australia: the RBA hiked 25bp as expected. Governor Bullock sounded incrementally less hawkish and said a hold had been discussed. Markets price about 35bp of hikes over the next year, the least in G10. GS economists expect an extended hold with upside risks. GS prefers AUD Z6U7 flatteners.

GS opened IRZ6IRU7 flatteners on 2 October 2026 (opened 0.19, latest 0.30, stop -0.05) and closed a long 3y SOFR swap spread trade for +5bp. Active trades: pay CHF 1y1y vs EUR 1y1y (+4bp), pay 5s on the 2s5s10s JGB fly (-3bp).

tension_points.bull_case: Spreads should tighten eventually and longer-dated spreads offer lower beta and yield protection. Energy relief, a successful French 2027 budget or an ECB policy response could stabilize OATs.
tension_points.bear_case: OAT-Bund spreads are at 2011-crisis levels, driven by risk premium beyond fundamentals, with spillover beta to Italy and other EGBs elevated. The ECB hurdle to use its balance sheet is high.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A shift in underlying macro or fiscal drivers is needed to stabilize spreads. Without energy relief or budget progress, spillover persists.

tension_points.bull_case: Dovish Fed speak, soft labor data and tighter financial conditions from wider credit spreads create an asymmetry toward lower yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Middle East uncertainty and resilient AI investment plans are upside risks to yields. Cheapening has extended into the belly of the curve.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The next US inflation print is the key test for the Fed path.
